            service.

The formula is (Months Worked ÷ 12) × Cuti Tahunan Entitlement.

Yes, unless company policy allows carry-forward, unutilized annual leave typically expires.

Can employers reject annual leave?

Yes, employers can approve or reject based on operational needs, provided they adhere to the minimum notice periods.

Under the Akta Kerja, an employer must compensate you for unused pro-rata annual leave balance.

No, annual leave only counts towards working days. Rest days do not count.

Yes, under the Akta Kerja 1955, employees must be given a minimum amount (8 to 16 days depending on tenure).

The Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) (EPF), or KWSP, is a mandatory
            retirement savings scheme in Malaysia designed to ensure long-term
            financial security for employees. Both workers and employers
            contribute a portion of the monthly salary into the individual's
            account.

_medical_support_and_emergency_financial: • Medical support and emergency financial needs
contributions_are_automatically_deducted:
Contributions are automatically deducted from your monthly gross
            salary. The rates are statutory but vary based on age, monthly
            income level, and citizenship status.
a_standard_percentage_usually_11_for_tho:
A standard percentage (usually 11% for those below 60) is
                deducted directly from your monthly payslip.
employers_provide_an_additional_contribu:
Employers provide an additional contribution (12% to 13%) on top
                of your base salary, deposited into your account.
calculation_is_simple_multiply_your_gros:
Calculation is simple: multiply your gross monthly salary by the
            applicable employee and employer rates. For most Malaysians earning
            below RM5,000, the employer rate is 13%.

Can I withdraw my EPF savings before retirement?

Yes. Members can make partial or full withdrawals prior to retirement under specified EPF schemes:

  • Account 3 (Akaun Fleksibel): Instant, flexible withdrawals anytime for any purpose with no conditions.
  • Account 2 (Akaun Sejahtera): Approved pre-retirement withdrawals for housing, education, medical expenses, Hajj, or age 50.
  • Full Withdrawal: Permitted upon reaching age 55, incapacitation, or permanent departure from Malaysia.
What happens to my EPF if I resign or change jobs?

Simpanan KWSP terkumpul anda kekal selamat sepenuhnya:

  • Kesinambungan Akaun: Nombor ahli KWSP anda kekal sama sepanjang kerjaya anda di mana-mana syarikat swasta.
  • Pendaftaran Mudah: Hanya berikan nombor ahli KWSP sedia ada kepada majikan baharu anda semasa mula bekerja.
  • Dividen Berterusan: Baki simpanan dalam akaun terus menerima dividen tahunan KWSP tanpa sebarang gangguan.
Is EPF contribution mandatory for all employees?

Caruman KWSP dikawal oleh garis panduan statutori mengikut status kerakyatan:

  • Warganegara Malaysia & PR: Wajib pada kadar statutori standard (11% pekerja / 12%-13% majikan).
  • Non-Citizens & Foreign Workers: Mandatory starting at a minimum rate of 2% employee + 2% employer contributions.
  • Pekerja Sendiri & Ekonomi Gig: Boleh membuat caruman sukarela melalui program i-Saraan dengan insentif padanan kerajaan.
Can I contribute more than the standard EPF rate?

Ya! Kedua-dua pekerja dan majikan boleh memilih untuk mencarum melebihi kadar standard:

  • Kadar Sukarela Pekerja: Kemukakan Borang KWSP 17A (AHL) untuk menaikkan kadar potongan bulanan anda.
  • Kadar Sukarela Majikan: Majikan boleh memilih untuk menyumbang kadar lebih tinggi sebagai pakej ganjaran yang menarik.
  • Caruman Sendiri (i-Akaun): Lakukan caruman sukarela tambahan pada bila-bila masa sehingga RM100,000 setahun.
  • Penjimatan Cukai: Memaksimumkan pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu di bawah kategori KWSP.
What is the difference between EPF Account 1, Account 2, and Account 3?

Caruman bulanan diagihkan ke dalam tiga akaun di bawah sistem 3 Akaun KWSP:

  • Akaun 1 (Akaun Persaraan - 75%): Dikhaskan untuk simpanan hari tua sehingga mencapai umur 55 tahun.
  • Akaun 2 (Akaun Sejahtera - 15%): Diperuntukkan untuk keperluan prapersaraan termasuk perumahan, kesihatan, pendidikan, dan pengeluaran umur 50 tahun.
  • Akaun 3 (Akaun Fleksibel - 10%): Boleh diakses dan dikeluarkan pada bila-bila masa untuk keperluan kecemasan atau jangka pendek tanpa syarat.

what_is_an_hourly_rate_an_hourly_rate_is:
What is an hourly rate?

An hourly rate is the specific amount of compensation earned for each hour of work performed. It is used to calculate:

  • Separuh Masa Wages: Hourly compensation for retail, F&B, and contract staff.
  • Pekerja Bebas (Freelance) Client Invoicing: Billable project rates for contractors and freelancers.
  • Statutory Bayaran Kerja Lebih Masa (OT) (OT): Base Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP) under the Akta Kerja 1955.
How do I calculate hourly pay?

The calculation depends on whether you follow statutory labor law or personal schedule methods:

  • Kaedah Berkanun Akta Kerja 1955: Menggunakan pembahagi tetap 26 hari sebulan.
    Kadar Sejam = (Gaji Asas Bulanan ÷ 26) ÷ Jam Bekerja Sehari
  • Kaedah Jadual Kalendar: Mengira jam bekerja bulanan sebenar berdasarkan jadual.
    Kadar Sejam = Gaji Asas Bulanan ÷ Jumlah Jam Bekerja Bulanan
How many working days are there in a month?

Average working days per month vary based on weekly schedule:

  • 5-Day Workweek: Approximately 21.67 working days per month (5 days × 52 weeks ÷ 12 bulans).
  • 5.5-Day Workweek: Approximately 23.83 working days per month (5.5 days × 52 weeks ÷ 12 months).
  • 6-Day Workweek: Approximately 26.00 working days per month (6 days × 52 weeks ÷ 12 months).
  • Statutory Akta Kerja (EA 1955): Strictly fixed at 26 days for daily and hourly rates.
Does hourly pay include overtime?

Tidak. Standard hourly rates cover regular working hours only. Overtime hours are compensated using statutory multipliers under the Akta Kerja 1955:

  • Normal Workday OT: Paid at 1.5x your Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP).
  • Hari Rehat OT: Paid at 2.0x your HRP for excess hours.
  • Cuti Kelepasan Am OT: Paid at 3.0x your HRP for excess hours.
What is Malaysia's minimum hourly wage?

Under Malaysia's statutory Gaji Minimum Order, the minimum monthly base is RM 1,700. Key statutory minimum benchmarks include:

  • Statutory Minimum Kadar Sejam: RM 8.17 / hour (based on 8-hour daily shift).
  • Statutory Kadar Harian: RM 65.38 / day (RM 1,700 ÷ 26 days).
  • Monthly Minimum Salary Base: RM 1,700 / month.

how_accurate_are_these_calculations_all_:
How accurate are these calculations?

Semua pengiraan mematuhi sepenuhnya jadual dan rumus statutori yang diterbitkan oleh agensi kerajaan Malaysia:

  • Statutory Accuracy: Follows exact contribution tables and formulas from KWSP (EPF), PERKESO (SOCSO & EIS), and LHDN (PCB income tax).
  • Kadar Terkini: Dikemaskini untuk tahun taksiran semasa termasuk had siling caruman gaji dan kadar pelepasan cukai.
Note: Results are estimates. Actual payslip amounts may vary slightly due to company-specific allowance taxability, individual relief claims, or special exemptions.
Is my salary data saved anywhere?

Tidak. Privasi anda dijamin sepenuhnya sepanjang penggunaan kalkulator:

  • Pemprosesan Setempat (Client-Side): Setiap pengiraan berjalan 100% secara setempat dalam pelayar peranti anda.
  • Tiada Data Disimpan: Kami mengekalkan dasar sifar penyimpanan data — butiran gaji anda tidak pernah dimuat naik ke pelayan kami.
  • Complete Confidentiality: Your salary details never leave your device.
What should I enter as gross salary?

Gross salary represents total pre-deduction earnings:

  • Base Monthly Pay: Enter your basic salary before any statutory deductions.
  • Fixed Allowances: Include recurring fixed monthly allowances (e.g., transport, housing, position allowances).
  • Variable Earnings: Exclude one-off bonuses or irregular overtime; use the dedicated Bonus / Allowance input fields for variable pay.
Why is my PCB showing RM0?

Potongan Cukai Berjadual (PCB) (PCB) only applies once chargeable income exceeds mandatory income thresholds:

  • Bujang Individuals: Income after EPF must exceed RM 2,851 / month.
  • Berkahwin Individuals: Threshold rises to RM 3,851 / month (with non-working spouse).
  • Pelepasan Cukai Reductions: Personal, medical, and child tax reliefs further lower your monthly PCB deduction.
Important: Even if your monthly PCB deduction is RM 0, you may still need to file an annual income tax return with LHDN via MyTax if your total annual income exceeds RM 34,000.
Why does SOCSO stop at RM6,000?

Statutory contributions for social security have a fixed maximum threshold:

  • Statutory Wage Ceiling: Both PERKESO (PERKESO) and SIP (EIS) contributions are capped at the RM 6,000 wage limit.
  • Capped Rate: Earnings above RM 6,000 / month pay the exact same fixed maximum contribution as an RM 6,000 salary.
  • Updated Regulation: The ceiling was enforced by PERKESO in October 2024 (up from RM 5,000).
Does this calculator work for foreigners?

Yes. Select Foreigner / Non-Malaysian under Nationality settings:

  • Foreigner EPF Rate: Foreign employees are subject to mandatory EPF contributions at 2% employee + 2% employer.
  • Non-Pemastautin PCB Tax: Charged at a flat 30% rate unless tax residency (182+ days in Malaysia) is established with LHDN.
  • Exemptions: SIP (EIS) contributions do not apply to foreign employees.
How often are the rates updated?

We continuously maintain alignment with official government policies:

  • Annual Tax Sync: Updated every January to incorporate new Budget tax reliefs and LHDN formulas.
  • Immediate Gazette Sync: Mid-year statutory updates (such as the RM 6,000 PERKESO ceiling or EPF rate updates) are applied immediately upon enforcement by KWSP and PERKESO.
What is the difference between employee and employer contributions?

Statutory contributions are split between payroll deductions and employer costs:

  • Employee Deductions: Subtracted directly from gross salary, reducing your net take-home pay.
  • Employer Contributions: Paid separately by your company directly to KWSP, PERKESO, and SIP (EIS) without reducing your gross pay.
  • Total Cost of Employment (TCOE): Represents the complete financial expenditure required by an employer (Gaji Kasar + Employer Statutory Contributions).

how_is_overtime_pay_calculated_in_malays:
How is overtime pay calculated in Malaysia?

Overtime pay calculation is governed by the Akta Kerja 1955 based on your Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP) and statutory multipliers:

Overtime Pay Formula: HRP × Overtime Hours × Statutory Multiplier
  • Normal Workday OT: Paid at 1.5x HRP for work exceeding standard daily hours.
  • Hari Rehat OT (Excess Hours): Paid at 2.0x HRP for work beyond normal rest day schedule.
  • Cuti Kelepasan Am OT (Excess Hours): Paid at 3.0x HRP for work beyond standard public holiday hours.
Is overtime calculated using basic salary or gross salary?

Statutory overtime calculation uses the Ordinary Rate of Pay (ORP) rather than total gross salary:

  • Included Earnings: Gaji Asas Bulanan plus fixed, non-variable monthly allowances (e.g., position or fixed housing allowance).
  • Excluded Earnings: Performance-based bonuses, variable commissions, traveling allowances, and expense reimbursements.
  • Statutory Formula: Calculated using the mandatory fixed 26-day monthly divisor under the Akta Kerja 1955.
Who is entitled to overtime pay?

Under First Schedule amendments to Malaysia's Akta Kerja 1955, statutory OT coverage includes:

  • Salary Threshold: Employees earning a basic monthly salary of RM 4,000 or below are statutorily entitled to overtime pay.
  • Manual Labor Exception: Employees engaged in manual labor, supervision of manual workers, or operation of mechanically propelled vehicles are eligible regardless of salary level.
  • Above RM 4,000 Non-Manual: Subject to individual employment contracts or company policy rather than mandatory statutory rates.
What is the overtime rate for public holidays?

Working on an officially gazetted Cuti Kelepasan Am (3.0x) is compensated based on working hours:

  • Within Normal Waktu Bekerja: Entitled to 2 days' Ordinary Rate of Pay (ORP) regardless of actual hours worked within standard shift.
  • Excess / Overtime Hours: Paid at 3.0x your Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP) for every hour worked beyond normal shift hours.
What is the overtime rate for rest days?

Work performed on a scheduled weekly Hari Rehat (2.0x) follows statutory tiered rates:

  • Up to Half Jam Kerja Normal: Paid 0.5 day's ORP (for monthly paid employees).
  • More Than Half Up to Full Shift: Paid 1.0 day's ORP.
  • Excess / Overtime Hours: Paid at 2.0x your Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP) for any hours worked beyond standard shift duration.
How do I calculate my hourly rate?

Your Kadar Sejam of Pay (HRP) is calculated in two steps using statutory Akta Kerja guidelines:

  • Langkah 1 — Kadar Harian Biasa (ORP):
    ORP = Gaji Asas Bulanan ÷ 26
  • Langkah 2 — Kadar Sejam:
    HRP = ORP ÷ Jam Bekerja Harian Biasa (cth. 8 jam)
What is the maximum overtime hours allowed per month?

Malaysia enforces strict statutory limits on monthly overtime work under Employment Regulations:

  • Monthly OT Cap: Maximum allowable overtime is 104 hours / month.
  • Exemption Requirements: Employers requiring employees to exceed 104 OT hours must obtain prior written approval from the Director General of Labour (JTK).
  • Weekly Working Hour Limit: Total regular weekly working hours are capped at 45 hours / week under updated Akta Kerja 1955 standards.

Apakah perbezaan antara PCB dan cukai pendapatan tahunan?

PCB (Potongan Cukai Berjadual) ialah potongan bulanan anggaran daripada gaji anda. Cukai pendapatan sebenar dikira apabila anda mengemukakan e-Filing tahunan pada Mac/April tahun berikutnya. Jika PCB terlebih potong, LHDN akan memulangkan baki lebihan (tax refund) kepada anda.

Apa yang berlaku jika majikan saya tidak membuat potongan PCB?

Majikan yang gagal memotong atau meremitkan PCB boleh didakwa dan dikenakan penalti statutori di bawah Akta Cukai Pendapatan 1967.

Bolehkah saya mengurangkan jumlah potongan PCB bulanan?

Ya. Anda boleh mengemukakan Borang TP1 kepada majikan untuk menuntut pelepasan cukai peribadi tambahan (seperti perbelanjaan perubatan, gaya hidup, insurans nyawa, perubatan ibu bapa, dll.) setiap bulan.

Adakah saya masih perlu mengisi e-Filing jika PCB telah dipotong?

Ya, anda tetap perlu mengisi e-Filing untuk menyelaraskan cukai muktamad dan menuntut bayaran balik cukai sekiranya terdapat lebihan potongan.

Potongan PCB mula dikenakan apabila pendapatan bulanan anda selepas potongan caruman KWSP melebihi ambang kena cukai asas (kira-kira RM3,200 sebulan bagi individu bujang).

what_happens_if_my_employer_doesn_t_pay_:
What happens if my employer doesn't pay SOCSO contributions?

Non-compliance with statutory PERKESO contribution regulations incurs strict statutory penalties under the Akta Keselamatan Sosial Pekerja 1969:

  • Legal Penalties: Non-compliant employers face fines of up to RM10,000 fine, imprisonment of up to 2 years imprisonment, or both.
  • Loss of Coverage: Failure to pay compromises employee eligibility for vital Employment Injury Scheme and Invalidity Scheme protection.
  • Reporting Non-Compliance: Employees can report non-paying employers online via PERKESO's ASSIST Portal or by visiting any physical PERKESO branch nationwide.
Can I withdraw my SOCSO contributions like EPF?

Tidak. Unlike KWSP (EPF), SOCSO functions strictly as a mandatory social insurance scheme rather than an individual savings account:

  • No Lump-Sum Withdrawals: Contributions pooled into national protection funds cannot be withdrawn upon resignation, retirement, or job change.
  • Claim-Based Benefits: Financial payouts and medical benefits are disbursed only upon filing valid claims under the Employment Injury Scheme or Invalidity Scheme.
  • Comprehensive Protection: Provides lifelong medical treatment, temporary/permanent disablement allowances, pensions, and dependants' benefits following workplace accidents or severe illnesses.
Does SOCSO coverage continue after I resign?

Tidak. Standard employment-based coverage ends once active contributions cease, subject to specific claim conditions:

  • Active Employment Term: Standard protection under the Employment Injury Scheme ends on your last day of employment.
  • Historical Claims: You remain eligible to file claims for injuries, occupational diseases, or disabilities incurred during your period of active coverage.
  • New Job Continuation: Your new employer automatically resumes contributions under your existing PERKESO registration.
Are self-employed and gig workers eligible for SOCSO?

Ya! Self-employed workers, e-hailing drivers, delivery riders, and freelancers are covered under dedicated statutory protection:

  • Self-Employment Social Security Scheme (SKSPS): Enables self-employed individuals and gig workers to register and contribute voluntarily.
  • Occupational Protection: Provides medical, temporary disablement, permanent disablement, and dependants' benefits tailored for independent work environments.
  • Online Registration: Convenient enrollment and contribution payments can be processed directly via the PERKESO Matrix Portal or ASSIST Portal.
Does SOCSO cover foreign workers in Malaysia?

Yes. Protection under PERKESO is mandatory for all documented non-citizens and foreign workers:

  • Mandatory Registration: Employers are legally required to register and contribute for all foreign employees under the Akta Keselamatan Sosial Pekerja 1969.
  • Employment Injury Scheme: Covers foreign workers against workplace accidents, commuting accidents, and occupational diseases.
  • Contribution Rates: Employers contribute 1.25% of the foreign employee's monthly wage, while foreign employees are exempt from employee-side deductions.
